anomalies.observed: On the EthernetAndPower sheet the SS2040FL isolation diode U6 is drawn with its anode (pin 1, triangle side) tied to the global net BAT+ (the summed system rail) and its cathode (pin 2, bar side) tied to the battery positive terminal U7. The diode therefore conducts from BAT+ into the cell and blocks current from the cell into BAT+.
anomalies.expected: The specification states U6 is the battery-feed isolation diode wired 'anode on battery (via U7), cathode on BAT+' so that the 18650 can power BAT+ while USB/adapter 5 V on BAT+ cannot back-feed into the raw cell. The build has the diode installed/connected in the opposite direction.

evidence.quote: EthernetAndPower.kicad_sch (page 7): U6 SS2040FL, pin 1 (anode) on the BAT+ label wire, pin 2 (cathode) on the wire to U7 '+' (battery); BAT- on U7 '-'.

U6 ... netlist: anode on battery (via U7), cathode on BAT+ ... the diode's evident function is to prevent USB/adapter 5 V from back-feeding current into the raw, uncontrolled 18650 cell when both are present

anomalies.impact: The board cannot be powered from the 18650 (the diode blocks the discharge direction), and when USB or the DC barrel jack is present current is allowed to flow into the uncontrolled cell (the exact back-feed hazard the diode was meant to prevent).

parsed.summary: Most of the schematic matches the specification (regulator topology, EPD boost/charge-pump parts and values, signal mapping, Q2 load switch, S1 reset, barrel-jack battery disconnect). The one clear deviation is U6: the battery-feed isolation diode is oriented backwards (anode on BAT+, cathode on the cell) relative to the specified 'anode on battery, cathode on BAT+', which would prevent battery power and allow adapter back-feed into the cell.
